learn.hook: All you need is a ball, some flat stones and your friends. Ready for lagori?
points: 'The Lagori Champions' is about children who play lagori, a traditional Indian game.
Lagori is played with a ball and a pile of flat stones.
It has other names too. In many places it is called pitthu.
Two teams play. One team knocks down the pile with the ball and tries to build it again. The other team tries to get them out with the ball.
Lagori needs good aim, quick feet and teamwork.

example.q: Read: It was the inter-school lagori match in Hubballi. Team Sunflower threw the ball and knocked down the pile of seven flat stones. Quickly, they began to stack the stones again. Team Mango tried to get them out with the ball. Just in time, Leela placed the last stone and shouted, "Lagori!" Team Sunflower won. Team Mango clapped and said, "Well played!" Question: How did Team Sunflower win?
steps: Team Sunflower knocked down the pile.
They stacked the stones again while Team Mango tried to get them out.
Leela placed the last stone just in time and shouted 'Lagori!'
example.answer: They rebuilt the pile of stones before Team Mango could get them out.

learn.reallife: Ask your parents or grandparents which games they played as children: gilli-danda, kho-kho, kabaddi or lagori?

games.title: The lagori match
items: The pile of stones fell down
Team Sunflower began to stack the stones

games.title: Lagori: true or false?
items: Lagori is played with a pile of flat stones and a ball.
These are the only things you need.
Lagori is played with a shuttlecock.
A shuttlecock is used in badminton, not lagori.
Two teams play against each other.
Lagori has different names in different parts of India.
For example, it is often called pitthu.
You need costly equipment to play lagori.
A ball and some flat stones are enough.

quiz.q: What do you need to play lagori?
options: A ball and a pile of flat stones
quiz.explain: Lagori is played with a ball and flat stones.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up lagori with other games

quiz.q: Story line: "Team Sunflower threw the ball and knocked down the pile of seven flat stones." How many stones were in the pile?
quiz.explain: The story says there were seven flat stones.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the number word

quiz.q: Story line: "Quickly, they began to stack the stones again." What did Team Sunflower do after the pile fell?
quiz.explain: They began to stack (pile up) the stones again.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'stack'

quiz.q: Story line: "Team Mango tried to get them out with the ball." What did Team Mango try to do?
options: Get the other team out with the ball
quiz.explain: Team Mango used the ball to try to get Team Sunflower players out.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up what each team was doing

quiz.q: Story line: "Leela placed the last stone and shouted, 'Lagori!'" Why did Leela shout?
options: She had finished building the pile
quiz.explain: She placed the last stone, so the pile was built again.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the shout to placing the last stone

quiz.q: In many parts of India, lagori is also called ___.
quiz.explain: Lagori is often called pitthu. Kabaddi, kho-kho and chess are different games.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all traditional games are the same game

quiz.q: What kind of game is lagori?
quiz.explain: Lagori has been played in India for a very long time.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what 'traditional' means

quiz.q: Which skills help a team win at lagori?
quiz.explain: You must aim the ball well and work together to build the pile.
quiz.mistake: Picks skills that are not used in the game

teach.ask: Gappu has never played lagori. Can you explain how the game is played?
teach.praise: Fantastic! Knock down the pile of stones with the ball, then build it again before the other team gets you out. Gappu wants to play!
teach.nudge: What things do we need? What does one team do to the pile, and what must they do next?

learn.hook: Team Mango lost, but they still clapped. Why do you think they did that?
points: A good sport plays fair and follows the rules.
A good sport is kind whether they win or lose. They say 'Well played!' to the other team.
A good sport helps a player who falls and respects the umpire or referee.
Useful words: opponent (the team you play against), captain (team leader), champion (winner), cheer (shout to encourage).
Opposites: win – lose, fair – unfair, start – finish.

example.q: Think it through: Team Mango lost the match but clapped and said 'Well played!' What does this show?
steps: Losing can make you feel sad.
Even so, they praised the winners.
Being kind to the other team after losing is sportsmanship.

learn.reallife: In school sports day, cheer for every runner, not just your friends. Shake hands after a match.

games.title: Sports words
pairs: the person who makes sure rules are followed

quiz.q: Team Mango lost but said, "Well played!" What does this show?
quiz.explain: Praising the winners after losing shows good sportsmanship.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only winners can be good sports

quiz.q: What does 'opponent' mean?
options: The person or team you play against
quiz.explain: Your opponent is on the other side.
quiz.mistake: Thinks opponent means a teammate

quiz.q: Which word is the opposite of 'win'?
quiz.explain: The opposite of win is lose.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word linked to winning

quiz.q: Which of these is fair play?
quiz.explain: Fair play means following the rules of the game.
quiz.mistake: Thinks winning matters more than rules

quiz.q: What is a champion?
quiz.explain: A champion is the winner.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word 'champion'

quiz.q: A player from the other team falls down. What should a good sport do?
quiz.explain: A good sport cares about every player, even opponents.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the other team does not matter

quiz.q: Which word means the same as 'cheer'?
quiz.explain: To cheer is to shout to encourage someone.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with the opposite meaning

quiz.q: Your team lost a match. Which sentence shows you are a good loser?
options: "I will never play with you again."
quiz.explain: Congratulating the winners is what a good sport does.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is fine to blame others after losing

teach.ask: Gappu's team lost and Gappu wants to throw the ball away and cry. What does being a good sport mean?
teach.praise: That's right! A good sport plays fair, is kind whether winning or losing, and says 'Well played!' Gappu is shaking hands now!
teach.nudge: What should Gappu say to the winners? Does a good sport follow the rules?

learn.hook: Leela placed the stone. Leela shouted. Can one little word join these sentences?
points: A conjunction is a joining word. It joins words or sentences.
'and' adds things together: I like kabaddi and kho-kho.
'but' shows something different or surprising: We were tired, but we kept playing.
'or' gives a choice: Do you want a ball or a bat?
'because' gives a reason, and 'so' gives a result: We won because we worked together. It was dark, so we went home.

example.q: Think it through: join 'Leela placed the last stone.' and 'Leela shouted "Lagori!"'
steps: Both sentences tell what Leela did, one after another.
We are adding one action to another.
example.answer: Leela placed the last stone and shouted "Lagori!"

learn.reallife: You use conjunctions all the time: 'Can I go out and play? I finished my homework, so I am free!'

items.text: We wanted to play, ___ it started to rain.
Do you want a ball ___ a bat?
Team Mango clapped ___ they respected the winners.
It was getting dark, ___ we went home.

quiz.q: Which word is a conjunction?
quiz.explain: 'And' is a joining word.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a joining word is

quiz.q: Fill in: "Leela was tired, ___ she kept playing."
quiz.explain: Being tired and still playing are different ideas, so we use 'but'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'so' when the ideas are different

quiz.q: Fill in: "Shall we play lagori ___ kabaddi?"
quiz.explain: We are choosing between two games, so we use 'or'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'and' or another word when there is a choice

quiz.q: Fill in: "Raju missed the bus ___ he woke up late."
quiz.explain: Waking up late is the reason, so we use 'because'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up reason (because) and result (so)

quiz.q: Fill in: "It was raining, ___ we played indoors."
quiz.explain: Playing indoors is the result of the rain, so we use 'so'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up result (so) and reason (because)

quiz.q: Join the sentences: "Meena has a ball. Meena has a bat."
options: Meena has a ball but a bat.
Meena has a ball because a bat.
Meena has a ball and a bat.
Meena has a ball so a bat.
quiz.explain: We are adding two things, so we use 'and'.
quiz.mistake: Picks a joining word that does not fit the meaning

quiz.q: Which conjunction gives a reason?
quiz.explain: 'Because' tells us why something happened.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the job of each joining word

quiz.q: Fill in: "Our team played well, ___ we did not win."
quiz.explain: Playing well and not winning are different, so we use 'but'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'so' when the ideas do not match

teach.ask: Gappu wrote: 'I was hungry. I ate a worm.' How can Gappu join these with a conjunction?
teach.praise: Brilliant! 'I was hungry, so I ate a worm.' Conjunctions are joining words. Gappu's sentences are holding hands!
teach.nudge: Which little word can join the two sentences? What do we call such words?
